caption:
Why you’re afraid to be more seen as an ambitious female entrepreneur, artist, creative…

When shame sits at the centre of your identity, healing work can often become about “fixing yourself”. 

Including what and how you will allow yourself to create. 

Instead of learning to make it increasingly safer to be yourself as you are in any given moment. 

That’s the pattern break. 

Hi I’m Meg, and if you’re an ambitious entrepreneur, artist, creative on a journey of building your confidence to be seen, make sure you’re following @megannicola_ for more content like this. 🥰

Nervous System Regulation | Healing From Shame | Being Seen Trying
author: Megs 🧚‍♀️ Creative & Emotional alchemist
transcript: The reason you don't create more of the things you actually want to create is because you do not know how to handle your fear. There is this massive misconception, particularly in the spiritual, self-development, self-help space, that fear is something to fix, it's something to overcome, and if you grew up as a hyper vigilant child, that falls right into your survival identity of constantly feeling like somehow you were broken, you're not enough, you're missing something. So what happens is, as a child who learned to kind of question whether there was something wrong with us is, is we kind of externalize this ideal identity that we think we need to become before we can have the things that we want to have. Which includes being able to create this creative vision that we have for our lives, that we know we are here to experience, share with the world, and be recognized for. And so a lot of us spend our entire lives waiting to feel ready, waiting to feel more confident, waiting to get rid of this imposter syndrome, or this insecurity, or this fear of being seen. Instead of building our capacity to feel the deep discomfort and fear that gets activated in our body, when we think about doing the things and creating the things that we want to create. Now because this ideal identity that's really a survival identity that we're like pining for, we're like, this is going to fix us, this is going to make us become the person that we should have been. Because it is not possible, because it is not a human-centric experience of life, aka that you're always confident, that you're always happy, that you always feel good, that you are always doing things that feel comfortable and within your skill set. You are literally setting yourself up for failure. And so that identity loops. And so you're constantly stuck in this waiting mode. That is why you procrastinate so much. That is why you over-edit. That is why creating the idea versus sharing it with the world feels much more attainable than actually letting yourself be seen. It is not actually because you are not ready. It's not because you don't feel good enough, or you've not healed enough, or you've not gotten rid of all your fears and insecurities. It is because you believe that you cannot do this by simply being yourself. So it becomes this vicious cycle of, I don't feel enough to be myself. I have this ideal version of myself I need to become, but I actually can't get there because that ideal version of me doesn't actually exist, because it's impossible. And then I loop. I'm not good enough. I can't get there. I have to wait. I'm not good enough. I can't get there. I have to wait. The pattern break comes from making it so safe to confront and actually sit and see your fears and start getting them on board and start actually accepting them and learning how to move through them, that you allow yourself to take action as the version of yourself in every single present moment, regardless of what discomfort is active for you. So if that resonated, hi, I'm Meg and I help ambitious female artists, creatives, dreamers, like yourself, how to make it safe to be seen by making it safe to be yourself. So if that sounds like you, make sure you head to the link in my bio to register for my upcoming masterclass or to check out my one-to-one sessions and six-week mentorship.
title: Stop Waiting to Feel Ready to Create
one_liner: Fear isn't something to fix — build capacity to act despite discomfort as your present self.
key_points: Hypervigilant children develop a survival identity that demands becoming an 'ideal self' before creating or being seen
Waiting to feel confident, healed, or fear-free creates a procrastination loop that never resolves
Over-editing and preferring ideation over sharing are symptoms of believing you can't show up as you currently are
The pattern break is making it safe to feel fear and take action anyway, in each present moment
